newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BULLIMORE SAYS HE FELT ECSTATIC WHEN RESCUERS TAPPED
British yachtsman, Tony Bullimore, says he felt ecstatic when he finally realised he was going to be rescued.
Mr Bullimore says he'd begun to lose hope of ever being found.
He says he thought he was dreaming when he first heard the tapping on the hull of his overturned yacht, before realising help was at hand.
The Australian navy frigate HMAS Adelaide plucked him from the freezing Antartic waters on early Thursday afternoon after five days trapped in his upturned yacht.
WIK CAUSING CONCERN AMONGST PASTORALISTS - NT GOVT
The Northern Territory government says the High Court's Wik decision is already causing concern amongst pastoralists, about what they can and can't do on their land.
The Queensland Government has told pastoralists they risk breaking the law if they make property improvements without consulting native title claimants.
Territory Lands Minister Mike Reed says he knows of one pastoral lease holder near Katherine who wants to sub divide his land, but is worried about compensation claims.
Mr Reed says the sub division into horticultural blocks would create economic activity and jobs.
GOVERNMENT WON'T BE PUSHED ON CAR TARIFF CALL
The Federal Government says it won't be rushing into a decision on the future of the car industry.
The comments follow the Ford Motor company's claim that seven-thousand Victorian jobs will be threatened if the Federal Government proceeds with reducing tariffs to five per cent.
That recommendation's been made in a majority report of the Industry Commission.

Acting Industrial Relations Minister Peter McGauran says a reduction to five percent, is by no means a foregone conclusion. Paul Noack from the manufacturing workers union says the Federal government needs to pay attention to the industry.
The final decision is expected in May.
MINING FREEZE LABELLED A DISASTER
Queensland's mining industry has described a freeze on new mining and exploration permits and leases on non-freehold land as a disaster.
This follows the High Court Wik decision which found that pastoral leases could co-exist with Native title, prompting legal opinion the same would apply to mining leases.
Queensland's acting Minister for Mines and Energy Di McCauley says a hold has been put in place to allow the implications of the Wik decision to be investigated.
Mining Council Chief Executive Michael Pinnock says it was what industry expected, but describes it as an "absolute disaster", particularly for far north Queensland.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
